observations: A large rounded head shape dominates the center, outlined in white, with two mismatched spiral eyes—one large and gold-coiled, one smaller and black-ringed—set asymmetrically on a tan face.
A spiky crown of black, purple, and yellow points rises from the top of the head, flanked by a dense background of zigzag lines, orange and red fields, and scattered blue dashes.
A wide horizontal band across the lower face holds a row of gold oval shapes, below which a blue-outlined rounded form and small circular marks continue the face structure.
reading: The face pushes forward from a background packed with zigzag and wave marks in orange, red, and yellow. Its two spiral eyes pull attention in different directions—one dense and golden, one spare and open—giving the face a lopsided alertness that reads as comic unease. The spiked crown and gold oval band add ceremony without resolving whether the mood is festive or unsettled.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #219 and nnxyz nnotb #221. Those two show a soft luminous mass and a tall arched figure respectively—making #220's close-cropped, spike-crowned face the most compressed and frontal of the three.

connections.reason: nnxyz nnotb #221 shares the same zigzag-filled background and a white-outlined central figure, but stretches vertically where #220 presses the face flat against the picture edge.

nnxyz nifty faces #0000 layers dense marks across the whole surface around a central constructed figure, offering a cross-collection contrast: darker ground and sharper angular marks against #220's warmer, rounder forms.

lookingQuestion: What does the difference in size and line density between the two spiral eyes do to how you read the face's expression?
ambiguities: The gold oval band across the lower face could be read as teeth, keys, or a decorative element—the image does not resolve this.
nnxyz nifty faces #0000 is from a different collection; the connection rests on inspected visual surface similarity, not sequence proximity.
